content.text: I reviewed the file — it's already well-built. I found one real bug: when a user's OS has `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, JS correctly starts paused and lets them click "Resume" to override — but a CSS media query separately force-pauses the animation regardless of JS state, so the resume button appears to do nothing (it shows "Resume animation" but nothing animates). I'll fix that so the JS state is the single source of truth, and tighten up wrapping of the hint text on narrow screens.

content.text: Since JS already initializes `manuallyPaused` from `prefers-reduced-motion` and adds `body.paused` accordingly, dropping the redundant CSS media query means the pause/resume button now actually works for users with reduced-motion enabled, instead of being stuck permanently paused.
